```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5)
has_quanteda <- requireNamespace("quanteda", quietly = TRUE) &&
  utils::packageVersion("quanteda") >= "4.5.0"
has_plot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
```

A word can occur six times in one opening unit or return in three different
units. Total frequency cannot distinguish those arrangements. This guide asks
**where selected words occur, and whether they return after their declared
teaching unit**. It connects saved concordance matches to a book's section
roster, then displays counts without losing absent targets or unobserved parts.

Use development **ldfreq 0.5.0.9001**, optional **quanteda >= 4.5.0**
for searching, and **ggplot2** for drawing. See the
[installation instructions](https://ryuya-dot-com.github.io/ldfreq/index.html#install).
Stable 0.4.0 does not include this example. The two helpers in
`examples/textbook-progression.R` are explicitly sourced installed examples,
not exported functions. The script also loads the unchanged concordance helpers.

## Begin with an inspectable example

```{r textbook-demo, eval=has_quanteda}
library(ldfreq)
demo <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "textbook-progression-demo.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), demo)
helper <- demo$helper
x <- demo$progression
x$summary[c("query_id", "occurrences", "first_observed_page",
  "last_observed_page", "observed_units_with_hits")]
```

These are authored texts for a 12-page, six-unit book, not actual textbook
observations or learner outcomes. `river` and `planet` both occur six times.
`river` occurs in Units 1, 3 and 5; `planet` occurs only in Unit 1.
`protect` is a declared target with no occurrences. Page 10 is a known blank
page. The example explicitly supplies lowercase lemmas and maps `recycled`
to `recycle`; it does not run an automatic lemmatizer.

```{r textbook-pages, eval=has_quanteda && has_plot}
helper$textbook_progression_plot(x, by = "page")
```

Each cell gives a count of saved matches. The default is colour; use
`monochrome = TRUE` for a grey scale with the same numeric labels.
Zero means no matches within the selected, completely observed scope.
`NA` means the exact count is unknown. An em dash means that no section on
that page was selected, whose contribution to the selected-scope total is zero.
Place figure numbers, titles and explanatory notes outside the plot.
Use a selected target list and an appropriate output width for long books;
the helper does not paginate or automatically suppress labels.

```{r textbook-units, eval=has_quanteda && has_plot}
helper$textbook_progression_plot(x, by = "unit", monochrome = TRUE)
```

The Unit view makes the same counts readable at a coarser scale. For a cumulative
count at each page or Unit, set `cumulative = TRUE`. This displays counts, not
a learning curve. The exact cumulative total becomes `NA` from the first
incomplete selected part onward; `observed_cumulative` in the table retains
the known-match lower bound without presenting it as the exact total.

## Supply your own book, order and target list

First prepare complete source-aligned annotations and call
`concordance_search()` as shown in
[concordance and dispersion](concordance-and-dispersion.html).
Use one document ID for one book, with a segment for each declared section.
Include punctuation in the annotation input before applying a search selection.
Do not replace missing text with an empty string. Import only the observed
sections; list the unobserved sections in the separate roster below.

| Table or argument | Required information |
| --- | --- |
| `search` | One unchanged concordance result for exactly one book. Patterns, lexical unit, exclusions, original text and occurrence IDs remain attached. |
| `sections` | One row per declared section: `document_id`, unique `segment_id`, positive whole-number `page` and `unit`, nonblank `role`, and logical `observed`. Rows follow page and Unit order. Multiple sections on a page are allowed; a page belongs to one Unit. |
| `targets` | One row for every saved `query_id`, including absent targets, and `introduction_unit`: a Unit in the roster or numeric `NA` when unknown. Row order sets the displayed target order. |
| `include` | One logical value per section, without missing values. The default includes all sections; an explicit mask can select body text, exercises or another declared scope. |

All and only `observed = TRUE` rows must match the saved source segments,
including their original order. Unobserved rows have no source segment.
Declare the complete intended page/section inventory: the helper cannot
detect omitted pages, OCR errors or an incomplete inventory from the text alone.
Page/Unit numbers are ordering coordinates, not automatically extracted
printed labels. Store edition, volume, printed labels, original files and
actual teaching dates alongside the analysis when needed.

```{r textbook-own-data, eval=FALSE}
helper <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "textbook-progression.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), helper)

# search was created from your complete observed source annotations.
progression <- helper$textbook_progression(search, sections, targets,
  include = sections$role %in% c("body", "exercise"))
helper$textbook_progression_plot(progression, by = "unit")
```

Use the supplied surface, lemma or another justified annotation as the search
unit. A word-family search needs an explicitly supplied mapping and a suitable
query; it is not inferred from spelling. Preserve the mapping and its source.
The existing search also supports multi-token queries. Matches cannot cross
section boundaries, so dividing the text at each page will exclude a phrase
split across a page break. This limitation must suit the intended analysis.
Overlapping or duplicated query patterns are counted separately; summing
different queries is not unique-word coverage.

The default `max_cells = 1e6` bounds the combined page-by-query and Unit-by-query
tables before allocating them. The search has its own allocation limits.
Neither bound guarantees a particular memory footprint or readable plot size.

## Distinguish absence, missingness and excluded sections

Suppose an exercise on page 7 has not been transcribed:

```{r textbook-missing, eval=has_quanteda}
s <- demo$sections
missing_exercise <- s[7, ]
missing_exercise$segment_id <- "p07-exercise"
missing_exercise$role <- "exercise"
missing_exercise$observed <- FALSE
missing_exercise$text <- NA_character_
s <- rbind(s[1:7, ], missing_exercise, s[8:12, ])
incomplete <- helper$textbook_progression(demo$search, s, demo$targets)
subset(incomplete$pages, query_id == "recycle" & page >= 7,
  select = c(page, observed_occurrences, occurrences, cumulative, status))
```

One occurrence is known on page 7, but the page total is unknown because the
exercise is missing. The helper retains that known occurrence and its original
context. Unit 4 and the whole-book exact total are also unknown. The observed
counts are lower bounds under the saved matching and annotation conditions,
not estimates of how many words would be found after correcting OCR or lemmas.

Missing or blank search annotations on retained tokens also make a selected
section incomplete. A deliberately excluded token is different: it defines
the search scope and does not by itself create missingness. An unobserved
section excluded by the explicit section mask does not invalidate the selected
scope either:

```{r textbook-scope, eval=has_quanteda}
body <- helper$textbook_progression(demo$search, s, demo$targets,
  include = s$role == "body")
stopifnot(identical(body$summary$occurrences, x$summary$occurrences))
```

These counts now describe body text only. They do not establish the absence of
additional practice elsewhere. Keep vocabulary boxes, instructions, answer
keys and indexes identifiable so that repeated printed words are not silently
treated as equivalent learning activities.

## Assess recurrence after a declared introduction

```{r textbook-followup, eval=has_quanteda}
x$summary[c("query_id", "introduction_unit", "later_units",
  "complete_later_units", "later_occurrences", "later_unit_coverage", "later_status")]
```

The reference point is the caller's **teaching introduction**, not automatically
the first occurrence. Later units are units strictly after it that have at least
one selected section. Thus within-Unit repetitions and later-Unit recurrence
are distinct. `later_unit_coverage` is the proportion of those later units with
at least one saved match, calculated only when every such unit is complete.
It is descriptive coverage, not a recycling-quality score.

In the example, `river` appears four times in two of the five later units.
`planet` has five observable later units but no further occurrences. `energy`
is introduced in the last unit: its later-unit count is zero and coverage is
`NA` with `no_later_units`, not a failed recycling score. An unknown introduction
produces `unknown_introduction`; missing material in the later scope produces
`incomplete_later_units`. Missingness confined to the introduction unit need
not invalidate the separate later scope.

`first_observed_page` and `last_observed_page` are the bounds of known matches.
If some material is missing, they need not be the actual first and last
occurrences. Different page or Unit lengths affect opportunities to encounter
words. Keep raw encounter counts for this question; comparing lexical
concentration additionally requires explicitly defined exposure denominators.
The existing within-document DP partitions original token slots, not these
page/Unit boundaries, and is not a substitute for the progression display.

## Return from counts to the original uses

```{r textbook-context, eval=has_quanteda}
subset(x$occurrences, query_id == "river" & included & unit > 1,
  select = c(occurrence_id, page, unit, role, pre, keyword, post))
```

The table retains all saved occurrences with an `included` flag; filter that
flag when explaining a displayed count. Original segment IDs, character spans,
contexts and occurrence IDs are unchanged. Reading those contexts can separate
the same sentence repeated from different senses, collocations or tasks.
Further pedagogical coding is a separate recorded judgment.

Repeated printed appearances indicate opportunities in the selected material,
not actual learner exposure, successful retrieval or vocabulary acquisition.
Page gaps do not measure elapsed teaching time. Neither a fixed repetition
threshold nor a widely spread pattern establishes effective spiral instruction;
the material, tasks and learning evidence must support that interpretation.

## Save and reopen without rerunning the search

```{r textbook-save, eval=has_quanteda}
record <- list(progression = x, session = utils::sessionInfo())
saved <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds") # Use a lasting private path for research data.
saveRDS(record, saved)
restored <- readRDS(saved)
stopifnot(identical(restored, record))
```

Keep the full record, including original text, roster, introduction choices,
queries and inclusion mask. The plot checks the saved record's integrity and
does not tokenize or search again. In a fresh R session:

```{r textbook-reopen, eval=FALSE}
library(ldfreq)
helper <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
sys.source(system.file("examples", "textbook-progression.R",
  package = "ldfreq", mustWork = TRUE), helper)
record <- readRDS("textbook-record.rds") # Your actual saved path.
record$progression$summary
helper$textbook_progression_plot(record$progression, by = "unit")
```

Reopening tables requires ldfreq's required packages; drawing also requires
ggplot2. No new quanteda search, parser or model is needed. Preserve the original
calculation session rather than replacing its versions with those of the
reopening session. Fingerprints detect accidental record changes; they do not
validate the correctness of source transcriptions, lemmas or teaching metadata.
